dataflow.name: SideSeeing: frames, segments and blocks
dataflow.description: A walk along the sidewalks of Chicago's West Loop, read in place from the SideSeeing bucket: a frame every 2 s, what each of 9 labels covers in it found by SAM 3, the frames placed on the walk's GPS track on a map, and the walk cut into blocks at the street corners it passes, each block with its share of frames showing each label.
dataflow.task: Find curb cuts and what stands in a walker's way along a sidewalk walk, frame by frame, and compare the blocks between its corners.

nodes.goal: Load the walk's video, read in place from the SideSeeing bucket.
Load the walk's GPS track, its gps.csv.
Load the West Loop's street corners.

nodes.content:
"""Sample Video Frames.

Input: a collection's rows, as Data Loading's `curio_load_collection(...)` returns
them. Every video row becomes one row per sampled frame, and each frame is a
JPEG written beside the collection's other derived files. A frame row has the
columns of an image row (`path`, `thumbnail`, `image_url`, `width`, `height`),
so Simple View shows the frames and any node that reads images reads them. It
also keeps the video's own columns: its fields, its position, and its time,
moved forward by the frame's offset. `t_s` is the frame's time in the video,
and `frame` its number there.

The Widgets tab sets the gap between two sampled frames, in seconds, and the
most frames kept from one video.
"""

from media_collections import sample_video_frames

return sample_video_frames(
    input_0, curio_derived_file,
    every_seconds=float([!! every_seconds !!]),
    max_frames_per_video=int([!! max_frames_per_video !!]),
)
nodes.goal: Sample a frame every 2 s over the whole walk.

nodes.content:
import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd

# The walk's GPS fixes, each at its time in the video: t_s is the fix's
# datetime_utc less the walk's taken_at, both in UTC.
listing, walk = input_0, input_1
fixes = pd.read_csv(listing["path"].iloc[0])
fixes["datetime_utc"] = pd.to_datetime(fixes["datetime_utc"], utc=True)
taken_at = pd.Timestamp(walk["taken_at"].iloc[0])
taken_at = taken_at.tz_localize("UTC") if taken_at.tzinfo is None else taken_at.tz_convert("UTC")
fixes["t_s"] = (fixes["datetime_utc"] - taken_at).dt.total_seconds()
return gpd.GeoDataFrame(
    fixes, geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(fixes["longitude"], fixes["latitude"]), crs=4326,
)
nodes.goal: Place each GPS fix at its time in the video.

nodes.content:
from sam3_images import find_in_images

# The Widgets tab sets what to look for, in plain words (SAM 3 takes any short
# noun phrase): here the 9 labels the SideSeeing walk example tracks, the ways
# a curb meets the street, what marks a crossing underfoot, and what stands in
# a walker's way. It also sets the score SAM 3 needs to keep an object, the
# widest images are read and drawn at, and the most images one run looks at.

return find_in_images(
    input_0, curio_load_model("model.curio.sam3"), curio_derived_file,
    labels=[!! labels !!], threshold=float([!! threshold !!]),
    width=int([!! width !!]), max_images=int([!! max_images !!]),
)
nodes.goal: Find what each of the 9 labels names in each frame.
Load the West Loop's streets and buildings from OpenStreetMap.

nodes.content:
import geopandas as gpd
import pandas as pd

# Where the walk is cut into blocks: the first time a GPS fix comes within 12 m
# of a corner of two named streets. A block runs along the street its corner
# shares with the next corner the walk passes, from its corner's other street
# to the next one's.
fixes, corners = input_0, input_1
near = gpd.sjoin_nearest(fixes.to_crs(26916), corners.to_crs(26916), max_distance=12)
passed = near.groupby(["street_a", "street_b"], as_index=False)["t_s"].min().sort_values("t_s")
passed = passed.to_dict("records")
cuts, street = [], None
for here, there in zip(passed, passed[1:] + [None]):
    names = {here["street_a"], here["street_b"]}
    if there is not None:
        shared = names & {there["street_a"], there["street_b"]}
        street = min(shared) if shared else None
        to = ", ".join(sorted({there["street_a"], there["street_b"]} - {street}))
    else:
        street = street if street in names else None
        to = "the walk's end"
    cuts.append({"street": street, "from": ", ".join(sorted(names - {street})), "to": to, "t_s": round(here["t_s"], 3)})
return pd.DataFrame(cuts)

Show each frame beside its overlay.
Chart the mean share of a frame each label covers.

nodes.content:
import geopandas as gpd
import numpy as np

# Each frame placed on the walk where the GPS track was at its t_s, between the
# fixes before and after it, with the share of the frame each label covers.
frames, fixes = input_0, input_1.sort_values("t_s")
shares = [column for column in frames.columns if column.endswith("_pct")]
placed = frames[["t_s", "dominant_class", *shares]].rename(columns=lambda column: column.replace(" ", "_"))
lon = np.interp(frames["t_s"], fixes["t_s"], fixes["longitude"])
lat = np.interp(frames["t_s"], fixes["t_s"], fixes["latitude"])
return gpd.GeoDataFrame(placed, geometry=gpd.points_from_xy(lon, lat), crs=4326)
nodes.goal: Place each frame on the walk, between its GPS fixes.

nodes.content:
"""Split Video.

Input: on the top circle, a collection's rows, as Data Loading's
`curio_load_collection(...)` returns them; on the bottom circle, if anything is
wired there, where to cut: one row per block, with `t_s`, where the block
starts in seconds from its video's start, and maybe `end_s`, where it ends, and
`video_file_id`, the video it cuts. Every video becomes one row per block, each
block an MP4 of its own that Simple View plays, with no sound. A block's row
leads with `block`, the cut's own columns (a street's name, say), `t_s` and
`end_s`, where the block starts and ends in the video, so a player linked by
time reads the video's time; then it keeps the video's own columns.

The Widgets tab sets the length of one block, in seconds, when nothing is
wired to the bottom circle; the widest a block is drawn, in pixels; and the
most frames one run re-encodes.
"""

from media_collections import split_video

return split_video(
    input_0, curio_derived_file, input_1,
    block_seconds=float([!! block_seconds !!]),
    width=int([!! width !!]),
    max_frames=int([!! max_frames !!]),
)
